speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and has there been any recent trauma or injury to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the time of injury, and are you currently unable to fully straighten the tip of your finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any visible deformity or a gap at the tip of the finger, and are you unable to actively flex the distal joint despite being able to move it passively? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your inability to actively flex the tip of the finger despite passive movement being possible, this strongly suggests a rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. I will now request medical images to visualize the soft tissue structures and confirm the tendon injury. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of an extended distal interphalangeal joint with an inability to actively flex it, combined with the mechanism of injury and the absence of fracture on X-ray, is classic for a jersey finger injury. DIAGNOSIS READY: Flexor Digitorum Profundus Tendon Rupture

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
